title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms — overview (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Charter guarantees democratic, mobility, legal, equality, and language rights, among others. Section 1 allows ‘reasonable limits’ demonstrably justified in a free and democratic society; section 33 (notwithstanding) applies only to certain rights and for renewable periods.

title: Federal division of powers (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: sections 91–95 allocate law-making authority between Parliament and provincial legislatures (e.g. criminal law federal; property and civil rights provincial). Paramountcy resolves some conflicts when both validly legislate.

title: Constitutional judicial review (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Canadian courts may declare laws of no force or effect to the extent of inconsistency with the Charter or federalism provisions. Dialogue with legislatures can occur through re-legislation within constitutional bounds.

title: Aboriginal & treaty rights (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: section 35 recognises and affirms existing Aboriginal and treaty rights, which are elaborated through negotiation, legislation, and litigation. Interpretation is highly fact- and nation-specific.
